messages:
carla: Heads-up — after the SA (sa-east-1) firewall tighten this morning, a bunch of new GPU nodes are failing to join the cluster. Seeing keystore/KMS errors and node registration timeouts.

mike: Oof. Is it the subnet-level rules or something on the keystore privatelink?

carla: Looks like the NACL + new outbound deny on 443 to central-keystore-prod is blocking the HSM proxy calls. Error from node: `KMS decrypt failed: AccessDenied` and `dial tcp 10.12.34.56:443: i/o timeout`.

anika: Can you paste the minimal log snippet?

carla: Sure — pasted from node bootstrap:```
2026-03-20T08:12:03Z ERROR keystore-client: decrypt key failed code=AccessDenied attempt=1
2026-03-20T08:12:04Z WARN runtime: registerNode: registration timed out after 30s
2026-03-20T08:12:04Z INFO network: dialing privatelink://central-keystore-prod:443 -> timeout
```

security: @carla thanks for the data. We tightened the outbound rules to comply with new regulator requirement (egress to unknown endpoints). We intended to whitelist the privatelink endpoint but maybe the CIDR changed.

ops-runner: Confirming — the keystore privatelink IPs rotated when we applied the internal CA renewal. We pushed the new CIDRs to the allowlist in EU/NA but missed SA. My bad.

mike: Plan: temporary rollback of the new deny in SA so nodes can join, then add the correct privatelink CIDRs + a more precise security group exception for keystore. Can we do rollback now?

deploy-bot: rollback firewall-rule/sa-tighten-2026-03-20 triggered by ops-runner at 08:33 UTC — in progress.

carla: Rolling back now. Node join rate picked up immediately for a few canary nodes. :thumbsup:

anika: Once rolling back, we should make a targeted IAM tweak so the keystore proxy returns AccessDenied less often for misrouted connections (defense-in-depth). Also need to update our audit logging to capture which CIDR caused registration failures.

security: Agreed. Two workstreams: 1) firewall fix + CIDR whitelist; 2) audit/logging retention and alerting so this is caught pre-rollout. Note: compliance asked for immutable audit retention for 13 months — that affects storage cost in SA.

mike: For immediate mitigation, ops-runner will add the correct privatelink CIDRs to SA allowlist and reapply a tightened rule with an exception for `privatelink-central-keystore`. Then we'll run a 5-node canary before full rollout.

ops-runner: Done. Added CIDRs, re-applied rule with exception, kicked canary. Nodes joined cleanly.

carla: We're back to green for cluster health. Tracking: join fail -> rollback -> CIDR fix -> canary -> reapply.

security: On audit costs: SA logs are ~1.8x per GB vs us-east. If we keep 13 months immutable retention there, the bill goes up. Proposal: route keystore audit stream to central US bucket with replication, set lifecycle + immutability there to satisfy legal, and keep only 90d raw in SA region. Legal to confirm.

anika: That sounds reasonable. Routing also helps correlate join failures across regions. ops-runner can we do a proof-of-concept for central routing?

ops-runner: Yes. I'll set up a logshipper pipeline to us-central-logs for keystore/audit and add a lifecycle rule. ETA for POC: 48 hours.

mike: Follow-ups: 1) postmortem stub, 2) add keystore privatelink CIDR to infra runbook, 3) add pre-rollout egress checklist to the firewall change PR template.

carla: I'll create the postmortem and link the logs. Will add checklist items to PR template.

sre-bot: Incident resolved at 08:51 UTC — service join errors decreased to baseline. Auto-close in 24h if no regression.

security: Thanks everyone. After the POC we'll sync with Legal about the retention approach before changing production retention. :eyes:
